name: Fender 6G15 Reverb (Accutronics 4AB3C1B tank)
description: Fender 'Reverb' Model 6G15, the stand-alone tube spring reverb, from the factory schematic and layout (H-FA). V1A 12AT7 (1 MOhm input, 100 kOhm + 10 kOhm plate load off +250 V, 1500 || 25 uF) feeds the DWELL 250 kOhm through .01 from the 100k/10k junction; V1B 12AT7 (100 kOhm, 1500 unbypassed) drives the 6K6GT grid through .002 / 220 kOhm; the 6K6GT (1000 Ohm 2 W || 25 uF, screen on the +295 V node) drives the 4AB3C1B tank through TR2 125A12A; V3A 7025 recovers the tank (1500 || 250 uF, 100 kOhm), the CUT OFF pedal grounds its grid; .1 -> TONE 50 kOhm (bottom .01 to ground) -> .00025 -> MIXER 250 kOhm top. Dry: the input jack through .05 into the V3B cathode follower (2.2M/2.2M bias, 100 kOhm cathode) and .1 into the MIXER bottom; the MIXER wiper is the output. Supply (cut at the +295 V node; the +250 V rail stays in the signal group so the start-up settle solves it exactly): TR1 68319-A HT, three selenium cells half-wave, 40 uF (+300 V) - 4 H choke - 40 uF (+295 V) - 10 kOhm 1 W - 40 uF (+250 V). The 6K6GT is the library card fitted to the RCA 6K6-GT curves (work/tube-curves/6K6GT). Notes: wave-e/fender-6g15-27000.notes.md

sources.title: Fender 'Reverb' Model 6G15 factory schematic AND layout drawing (H-FA), two pages, read at native resolution (1512x870, 1426x988) in 2-3x crops: every value and connection, and the voltage annotations +105/+1.8, +120/+2, +285/+24, +160/+1.2, +120/+130/+250, +300/+295/+250 V (+-20 %) used as DC targets. The layout settles the 1000-2W cathode resistor, the 100k/10k Dwell divider, the 250K-L pots and the capacitor-input filter

Fender '63 Reverb Reissue service manual, June 1994 rev A, PR 263: theory of operation (V1A divider into the Dwell, CUT OFF grounds V3A's input) and parts list (1 kOhm 2 W driver cathode R10, .01 C9, 220 uF C7, 250k B / 50k B pots). Cross-check only: the reissue's driver is a 6V6
RCA 6K6-GT data sheet: 92CM-4881R2, 92CM-5209R2, 92CM-6311R1 and the typical-operation table, digitised to work/tube-curves/6K6GT (the library 6K6GT card)
Hammond 1750AX data sheet (replacement for Fender 125A12A): 7500:8 Ohm, DCR 345/0.699 Ohm, 6.0 H, 423 mH leakage; 125A12A turns 30.15:1 measured on an original (ampgarage.com 6G15 thread)
Hammond 290WX data sheet (replacement for Fender 68319A): HT 237 V / 50 mA, 255.9 V open circuit, DCR 22.92 / 182.6 Ohm

Catalogue unit 27000 mapping: Wet -> MIXER, iM -> CUT OFF pedal, L (High Damp) -> TONE inverted; Tm, SpringLength, B, H legacyOnly (one fixed 4AB3C1B, no size/length/bass/damping controls); Pwr host bypass; Dwell has no catalogue parameter. The catalogue's '3-spring' wording is the legacy description: the 6G15 used a 4AB3C1B two-spring long tank

lte.note: LTE substeps start on BDF2 (docs §10.61): the backward-Euler restart of every continued sample left a 96 kHz base-periodic line (300 Hz at -58 dB re the 2.9 kHz tone, under the hum mask). Engine 8x fine-step truth at the tank drive (tk), audio band, lead / rock DI: 0.692 / 1.298 % -> 0.693 / 0.885 %. CPU equal (9900X)

SEL3.note: three series selenium cells as three identical silicon junctions: the 1N4001 card (is 14.11 nA, n 1.984, rs 0.0339) with n and rs tripled

controls.label: Dwell
controls.note: DWELL 250K-L across the .01 from the V1A divider, bottom grounded, wiper to V1B's grid: the tank drive level. Linear taper: the sheet's '-L', and the '63 Reissue's 250k B. No catalogue parameter: set by id

controls.label: Tone
controls.note: TONE 50K-L: V3A's plate through .1 into the pot's top, its bottom through .01 to ground, wiper through .00025 into the mixer: a treble cut on the reverb return only. Answers the catalogue's High Damp (L) inverted (High Damp 0 = Tone full up, bright), which is the same function on the legacy tank: the return's high-frequency loss

controls.label: Mix
controls.note: MIXER 250K-L: wet (tone wiper through .00025) on one end, dry (cathode follower through .1) on the other, wiper to the output jack. 0 = dry only, 1 = wet only. Linear taper (sheet '-L', '63 Reissue 250k B). Catalogue Wet (Mix)

controls.label: Cut Off (footswitch)
controls.note: CUT OFF PEDAL: grounds V3A's grid (the tank's return), so 1 = reverb cut off, 0 = on. Catalogue iM (Mute)

controls.label: Size
controls.note: legacyOnly: the 6G15 has one fixed 4AB3C1B long two-spring tank; no size parameter exists

controls.label: Spring Length
controls.note: legacyOnly: one fixed long tank, no selectable spring length

controls.label: Bass
controls.note: legacyOnly: the 6G15 has a Dwell, a Tone and a Mix; no bass control. The fixed bass loss is the 250 pF / tone network and the tank's own roll-off

controls.label: Low Damp
controls.note: legacyOnly: the 6G15 has no damping control; the tank's decay is the 4AB3C1B's own

controls.label: On/Off
controls.note: Host bypass. The 6G15 has no bypass switch of its own: it is an always-on outboard unit, and its CUT OFF pedal is the 'mute' control above

parts.label: TR1 68319-A HT winding (open-circuit EMF)
parts.note: Fender 68319-A: the sheet prints no secondary voltage. Hammond lists its 290WX as the drop-in replacement for 68319A: HT 237 V at 50 mA, 255.9 V open circuit at 120 V mains -> 361.9 V peak EMF. The winding resistance is RPT. The sheet's own +300 V at the rectifier is the check (see notes)

parts.label: TR1 HT winding resistance + reflected primary
parts.note: Hammond 290WX DCR: HT 182.6 Ohm + primary 22.92 Ohm x (255.9/120)^2 = 104.2 Ohm reflected

parts.label: Selenium stack, three cells in series (half-wave)
parts.note: The sheet draws three selenium cells in series. Modelled as three identical series junctions (one D with n and rs tripled, which is exact for identical cells) on the 1N4001 card: selenium drops ~1 V per cell where silicon drops ~0.7 V, a ~1 V difference on 300 V; selenium reverse leakage is not modelled

parts.label: 40-450 reservoir at the rectifier (+300 V)
parts.note: Capacitor-input filter: the sheet draws this 40 uF on the rectifier side of the choke, with the +300 V annotation pointing at that node, and the second 40 uF after the choke at +295 V

parts.label: Filter choke DCR
parts.note: The 6G15 choke is given as Fender 125C3A (Hammond's own 6G15 listing, the 194A replacement) or 125C1A by different sources; both are 4 H. 167 Ohm is the Hammond 194A (125C3A) DCR, which reproduces the sheet's 300 -> 295 V drop at the unit's ~29 mA (4.8 V); the 125C1A's 110 Ohm would give 3.2 V

parts.label: 40-450 after the choke (+295 V): 6K6GT plate (via TR2) and screen
10 kOhm 1 W dropper to the +250 V preamp rail
V1A input stage (+105 V plate, +1.8 V cathode)
10 kOhm from the plate load to +250 V
parts.note: Both factory drawings (schematic and layout) put the 10 kOhm between the 100 kOhm plate load and the +250 V eyelet 'A', and take the Dwell feed from their junction; the '63 Reissue theory of operation describes the same divider ('The voltage divider R2 and R3 reduce the voltage so the overall gain is about 3')

parts.label: V1B driver stage (+120 V plate, +2 V cathode)
1500 cathode resistor, unbypassed
parts.note: The sheet draws no bypass capacitor on V1B (+2 V cathode) and the layout has none at that eyelet; the '63 Reissue likewise bypasses only V1A (C2) and the driver (C4)

parts.label: 6K6GT reverb driver (+285 V plate, +24 V cathode)
Cathode resistor 1000 Ohm 2 W
parts.note: Read as 1000 Ohm 2 W: the layout drawing prints '1000-2W' at that eyelet in clear lettering, and on the schematic the vertical '2W / 1000' label is what earlier passes read as 240/250. 1 kOhm is the value the printed +24 V needs (24 mA of cathode current, consistent with the 6K6GT card at this screen voltage), and the '63 Reissue uses a 1 kOhm 2 W (R10) in the same place

parts.label: TR2 125A12A reverb driver transformer (~7.3 kOhm : 8 Ohm)
parts.note: Turns 30.15 : 1, measured on an original 125A12A (Amp Garage 6G15 thread, impedance ratio 909:1 = 7.27 kOhm on 8 Ohm). DCR 345 / 0.699 Ohm, primary 6.0 H, leakage 423 mH from the Hammond 1750AX data sheet (the replacement Hammond designed to the original). lsat 0.6 V*s is an assumption: above the 0.52 V*s peak flux of the 1750AX's rated 3.5 W at 70 Hz, which it passes at under 1.5 % THD. The plate's 285 V (sheet) against the 295 V node is consistent with ~345 Ohm at ~26 mA

parts.label: Accutronics 4AB3C1B tank (input coil on TR2, output to V3A's grid)
parts.note: The drive is permanently connected: the CUT OFF pedal does not open it. The tank output coil is V3A's only grid return (the sheet draws no grid leak)

parts.label: CUT OFF PEDAL (shorts V3A's grid to ground)
parts.note: The pedal's jack tip is wired to the reverb-return line at V3A's grid and the pedal switch grounds it (sheet); the '63 Reissue: 'The footswitch turns the reverb on and off by grounding the input to the reverb recovery circuit'

parts.label: V3A 7025 reverb recovery (+160 V plate, +1.2 V cathode)
250-6 cathode bypass
parts.note: Labelled '6' and '250' on both drawings: read as 250 uF 6 V, the Fender value-voltage order, a 6 V rating suiting a +1.2 V cathode; the '63 Reissue fits 220 uF 16 V (C7) here

parts.label: .01 from the TONE pot's bottom to ground
parts.note: Both drawings print .01 here (the earlier pass had 0.1); the '63 Reissue's C9 is .01 too

parts.label: .00025 tone wiper to the MIXER top
Tone-wiper DC bleed
parts.note: the TONE wiper sits between the .1 and .00025 capacitors and has no DC path of its own; 1 GOhm stands in for their leakage so the node's operating point is defined

parts.label: Amplifier input the unit drives (1 MOhm)
parts.note: the 6G15 is an outboard unit plugged into an amplifier's 1 MOhm input; that load is the output node's DC path (the mixer sits between two coupling capacitors). Added as the unit's specified load, not a part of the unit

parts.label: .05 dry feed from the input jack
V3B 7025 cathode follower (grid +120 V, cathode +130 V, plate on +250 V)
